epaint 0.36.2 from crates.io, with right-to-left text ported onto it.

Why
egui 0.36.2 lays right-to-left runs out left to right, so Arabic and Hebrew
words come out mirrored and the caret gets lost in them (egui issue 8576).
The fix upstream is egui pull request 8577, still an unmerged draft on
2026-09-30, written against egui main, whose text code has moved on since
0.36.2. This folder is 0.36.2 with that work ported onto it, used through
[patch.crates-io] in the workspace Cargo.toml. Drop the folder and the patch
line once an egui release lays out bidi text.

Taken from pull request 8577
Commit c55da0337f67616ee7be4bfb06b73fdd71ef7f91, adapted to 0.36.2, which
has a Font in font.rs where the pull request has FontsImpl, and no
TextRun::raster:
- bidi levels per layout job with unicode-bidi, the paragraph direction from
  its first strong character
- runs split where the level changes, each shaped in its own direction
- Glyph::bidi_level and Glyph::is_rtl
- each row put in visual order after line breaking (UAX #9 rule L2), glyphs
  kept in logical order so a glyph's index is still its char index
- alignment, backgrounds, underline and strikethrough walk the glyphs by x
- the overflow character takes the level of the glyph before it
- its three tests, run on IBM Plex Sans and Plex Sans Arabic from
  assets/fonts instead of egui's default fonts

Not taken: commit c93e8863e958507056415e2a6dace56e23ba5f3a, which draws a
cluster with more glyphs than chars as one bitmap. IBM Plex Sans Arabic, the
only right-to-left font Booth ships, shapes no character into more glyphs
than characters. Checked on 2026-09-30: every character in its cmap, alone
and in its joining forms, letters with vowel marks, and every code point up
to U+2FFFF alone, after a Latin letter and after an Arabic one, with Plex
Sans first as the app has it; nothing in the Arabic blocks. The dotted
circle the shaper adds under a mark with no letter before it is turned off
instead (below). Nor the pull request's change to egui's selection painter:
egui-wgpu draws the flipped rectangle anyway.

Plex Sans, the Latin face, does give more glyphs than chars for 179 letters
it has no glyph of its own for, which the shaper builds from a letter and
its accents: among them the dotted letters of Arabic transliteration (for
example U+1E25, U+1E63, U+1E0D), U+01E7 and U+021E, some Cyrillic, and
polytonic Greek. That is 0.36.2's behaviour and is left as it is here; the
caret, the selection and the copied text after such a letter are one place
off. Commit c93e886 is what fixes it.

Changed from the pull request
- A right-to-left run is walked from the end of the shaper's output. The
  shaper puts a vowel mark before its letter; walked backwards it follows
  it and moves with it when the row is mirrored.
- In a right-to-left run the shaper's x offset goes into the glyph's image
  offset, so each glyph sits on its pen and joined letters stay joined when
  the row is mirrored.
- The n-th glyph of a cluster stands for its n-th char, so a letter and its
  mark each keep their own char.
- Row::x_offset: where the level changes the caret goes with the higher
  level, so after "123" or "hello" at the end of an Arabic line it follows
  the last digit or letter instead of the right end of the row, where the
  line starts. A caret between a letter and its marks sits at the letter's
  far edge.
- Row::char_at takes the nearest caret place, and on a tie one that is not
  between a letter and its marks.
- A row with no right-to-left glyph keeps 0.36.2's char_at and x_offset.
- Shaping asks for no dotted circle under a mark that has no letter before
  it: the circle would be a glyph without a char.
- UAX #9 rule L1 before rows are put in visual order: whitespace at the end
  of a row, and a tab with the whitespace before it, take the paragraph's
  level, so the space where a line wraps ends the row instead of sitting
  between two runs. The formatting characters rule X9 removes keep the level
  of the char before them (section 5.2), also after a tab. A right-to-left
  paragraph that an override made all left to right goes through this too.
- A zero-width glyph moves with the glyph before it only when both have the
  same level, so a direction mark or a control of another level still
  separates the runs around it. A block that does not advance takes no
  width, so a joiner that rule L1 moved does not take its letter's.
- The room a section's leading space or letter spacing leaves between two
  blocks moves as a space char there would, so it stays between the two
  sections and never lands inside a word.
- A space between two right-to-left words stays in their run when their
  face has a space, instead of each word and each space being a run of its
  own, shaped one by one. Laying out a 200-message Arabic chat at a new
  width went from 11.6 ms to 4.5 ms.
- A row with right-to-left text is as wide as its glyphs reach once it is
  in visual order. A vowel mark has no width and sits at the left edge of
  its letter, and the row's width came from its last glyph in logical
  order, or, when aligned, from the glyph placed rightmost; either could
  be a mark, and the row came out a letter short. A right-aligned
  Arabic message whose first letter carries a mark stuck out of the chat
  column, and out of its label, by that letter: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ
  was 76 wide with ب ending at 79.29. Aligned, such a row's box is rounded
  out to whole pixels when they fit its line, so right-aligned it ends on
  its edge instead of up to half a pixel past it, and its text sits up to a
  pixel further left. Put on whole pixels in visual order, a row can come
  out a fraction of a point wider than its line, as it could before this
  change: 300.24 on a line of 300. Rounded out to 301, the galley's rect
  was cut back to 300 on the right when the galley was rounded, a pixel
  short of the edge the row is aligned to, and a right-aligned label drew
  the row a pixel left of itself. Such a row keeps its own width and is
  placed as 0.36.2 places any row wider than its line: right-aligned, it
  ends up to half a pixel past its edge, or, when it is half a pixel or
  more too wide, its rect is cut back the same way and its last letter
  starts up to a point left of its label.
  PlacedRow::rect_without_leading_space starts such a row at its leftmost
  glyph instead of its first, which can be on the right.
- The overflow character that ends a cut row goes where the last letter
  ends when the char before it is a right-to-left mark. It went where the
  mark is, over the letter, and mirroring the row then put letters over
  each other, as when the room panel cuts a long name short.
- Thirteen more tests: the caret at the end of a line ending in digits,
  the caret staying with the run it was typed into, marks on their letters
  and joins, caret places round-tripping through x, the order unicode-bidi
  gives, Arabic words in one run, the space where a line wraps, a
  section's leading space, zero-width chars taking no room, a right-to-left
  row as wide as its first letter with a mark on it, one a little past its
  line starting where the galley does, English then Arabic with marks as
  wide as its letters, and an ellipsis after a mark.

Still as in 0.36.2
The arrow keys move by char index, in logical order, so Left moves right
inside Arabic. The selection highlight is drawn by egui, not here; the
vendored egui next to this crate draws it per run of selected letters (see
vendor/egui/PATCHED.txt).

Other changes to the crate
- Cargo.toml: unicode-bidi =0.3.18 added. The dev-dependencies (criterion,
  mimalloc, similar-asserts) and the benchmark removed: none of them is in
  Booth's Cargo.lock, and cargo will not test a crate outside the workspace
  that has dev-dependencies. src/text/fonts.rs uses assert_eq! where it used
  similar_asserts::assert_eq!. The comment cargo puts at the top when it
  publishes a crate is gone too; Cargo.toml.orig is still the original.
- src/text/fonts.rs: the FontDefinitions doc example is marked ignore; it
  includes a font by a path inside egui's own repository.
- The 13 upstream tests that need egui's default fonts are ignored unless
  the default_fonts feature is on. Booth does not build that feature, and
  the epaint_default_fonts crate is not in its Cargo.lock.
- The 13 long dashes in upstream comments replaced with plain punctuation.
- The emoji in 5 upstream comments replaced the same way, by words, a code
  point or nothing.
- The emoji in string and char literals, and one en dash, are kept but
  written as \u{...} escapes: in src/text/font.rs the en dash, U+203C
  and U+2049 among the chars a CJK line may not start with, in
  src/text/fonts.rs the white square drawn for a missing glyph, and in
  src/text/text_layout.rs one test string. The values are the same;
  checked on 2026-10-02 by compiling every changed literal against the one
  it replaced.
- In comments some stock phrases are put more plainly, and one debug
  assertion's message is reworded.
- Everything else is as upstream wrote it, its TODO lines included.

LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE are egui's, from github.com/emilk/egui at tag
0.36.2.

Tests: cargo test -p epaint --locked, from the workspace root.
